For reference, I just realized this got broken in 9.0.7 because of #36089. Prior to that PR, ngcc was able to process a bundle that it assumed to be UMD but actually contained ESM5 because the UMD handling used to be a superset of ESM5. We had this error as well in a big project being updated from Angular8 to 9.1.2, but only from the code where we use one particular service. It would intermittently give either the JIT error mentioned here, or sometimes an "Error: Cannot instantiate cyclic dependency!".

There is already a GitHub issue about the latter in #35225, and a comment [there](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/35225#issuecomment-583741461) about the depth of import statements having an impact, led us to the workaround:

The service causing the problem had both a * import and a reference to the dist path of the same package, i.e.
```
import * as models from '@gandalf/serverapi';
... more imports
import { MedlemApi } from '@gandalf/serverapi/dist';
```
We have long considered this an anti-pattern (but it worked in Angular < 9) and by removing the last line and instead reference the item with the models. prefix, e.g. `models.MedlemApi`, everything was working perfectly again.

Since this used to work, and because of the somewhat random and obscure error messages, I would prefer a fix for this scenario as well. But in the meantime, I hope this helps others with the same problem.

For people still seeing this issue: it is typically caused by one of these reasons:

1. libraries that are packaged in an unusual way such that ngcc is unable to process them to become Ivy compatible. Therefore, there's no singular root cause, each of the misbehaving libraries might need a different solution, or might not be supported at all (for example, minified bundles cannot be supported). The tricky part is figuring out which library is failing to be processed, analyzing the stack trace may help here.
2. The ngcc compiler is has not been run. When using the CLI this should all happen transparently, however custom build setups may need to be updated to run ngcc manually.

For the first case, please try to figure out what library is a problem, then seeing if an updade is available or whether there's an open issue with that library. If you can't find any of that, please open a new issue here with a reproduction repo, preferably using a minimal Github repro.
